messages:
sam: Heads-up — p99 latency started trending up at 16:02 UTC after the runtime push. We're missing the 1.2s SLO on several low-latency routes. Logs + graphs point to continuous-batcher wait times spiking. GPU util still high (~86%) but batches are sitting waiting for the max_batch_size to fill.

olivia: Can you paste the metrics you're seeing? is this the chat-generation models only or embeddings too? :thinking_face:

sam: Mainly chat-gen (r/medium model family). Quick numbers: p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.1s (SLO 1.2s). batch_fill_time p99 = 1.3s, average batch_size = 40, max_batch_size configured = 64, target_batch_fill_policy = continuous. queue_length_shard_x hit 120 reqs.

raj: That pattern sounds like "wait-for-fill" latency — continuous batching tries to optimize throughput but when throughput is bursty and max_batch_size is high it holds requests too long. We saw similar on us-west last year when model traffic had long tail.

sam: Right. Also noticed admission controller isn't rejecting or shedding; it keeps enqueueing, so latency piles up. GPU scheduling is OK but end-to-end latency gets dominated by batching waits.

dana: Customer-facing alerts triggered. Product asked for mitigation ASAP; can we do a hotfix that favors latency over throughput for the affected routes?

olivia: Immediate mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_size for that model shard 2) set max_wait_ms (batching window) to a low value 3) apply per-route admission caps (rate-limit) for non-critical clients. Any of those we can do now?

sam: I can roll a config patch: set max_batch_size: 24 -> 16, max_wait_ms: 20ms -> 8ms, and set batch_policy: latency_first for route /v1/chat. Quick diff:
```
# runtime batching config
model: r/medium-gen
batching:
  continuous: true
  max_batch_size: 16
  max_wait_ms: 8
  policy: latency_first
```
I'll canary this to 10% of capacity.

raj: Scaling nodes helps but takes 15-30m to warm and is expensive. If this is caused by policy, config change is fast and cheaper. Also recommend adding queue_depth_based_admission: reject if queue > 80 per-shard to stop unbounded queuing.

olivia: Agreed. Also add a short-term circuit to bypass batching for requests with header X-low-latency=true. That way PLG customers can opt out.

sam: Deploying canary now. CI link: https://deployments/redwood/canary/1749804523 (deploy started).

ci-bot: Canary deployment started for runtime-config patch (canary=10%). Logs: https://logs/1749804523.

olivia: Monitoring p99 on the canary pods. If we see p99 drop under 1.2s in 5m, ramp to 50% then 100%. If not, rollback.

dana: Keep me posted. I'll update support playbook with the temporary header trick and note expected customer impact.

sam: Canary p99 fell to 0.9s after patch on canary pods (5m). queue_length_shard_x down from 120 -> 18. Rolling to 50%.

raj: Follow-ups: (1) add dynamic max_batch_size that scales with request rate (2) implement queue-aware admission controller (3) cost analysis — throughput vs latency tradeoff per-customer, add per-tenant QoS. I'll own infra design doc.

olivia: I'll open an incident follow-up to capture RCA and the config changes. Short term postmortem + runbook.

sam: Thanks team. Plan: hotpatch pushed, follow-up RFC for dynamic batching/admission control, and product to decide default latency vs throughput for routes. :white_check_mark:
